answer.rationale: P99 write latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic. The release cannot be rolled back due to compliance constraints. Adding capacity takes time we don't have; circuit breakers would shed load and risk writes. memory_b5 demonstrates that routing read queries to replicas directly reduced primary load and recovered write latency the same day. This action: (1) preserves the mandatory security patch, (2) relieves primary write pressure without shedding customer transactions, (3) has proven precedent in our operational history, (4) is executable immediately. We verify memory_b5 to confirm the specific latency recovery pattern and ensure the read-replica routing mechanism is still operational. The write path remains on primary; we only offload reads, protecting settlement writes during peak.
